full_text_en:
Fenzhou Yuyuan Local Specialty Products Co., Ltd. v. Shaanxi Tianbao Soybean Food Technology Research Institute — dispute over technology contract

Ruling Summary

1. Whether a product that conforms to the contractual specifications can be produced is not on the same level as whether the product can be marketed and sold, whether it is marketable, or whether there is a profit margin. In the field of technology contracts, especially contracts involving technology industrialization, if there is no explicit agreement between the parties, the commercialization of the product should not be regarded as the purpose of the technology contract.

2. An investor should carefully enter into contracts involving technology industrialization. In setting technical indicators and selecting product acceptance standards, the investor should, to the extent possible, align them with market requirements for the product. In particular, in areas with intense market competition or higher public expectations, the investor should avoid using only market access standards as the product acceptance standards under the contract, thereby avoiding the predicament where the product is compliant but the business fails.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2016) Zui Gao Fa Min Zai No. 251

Re-Applicant (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Shaanxi Tianbao Soybean Food Technology Research Institute. Address: Room 10405, Unit 4, 1st Floor, Ruishi Building, No. 58 Keji Yi Road, High-tech Zone, Xi'an, Shaanxi Province.

Legal Representative: Guo Kai, Director of the Institute.

Agent ad litem: Zhao Zhijie, employee of the Institute.

Agent ad litem: Pan Xiaoping, lawyer of Shaanxi Yongjiaxing Law Firm.

Respondent (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Fenzhou Yuyuan Local Specialty Products Co., Ltd. Address: Yuyuan Industrial Park, West Exit of Fenjun Expressway Fenyang, Fenyang City, Shanxi Province.

Legal Representative: Yu Cuiping, Chairwoman of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Jin Erlan, lawyer of Shanxi Boyuan Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Wang Yanbiao, lawyer of Shanxi Boyuan Law Firm.

The re-applicant, Shaanxi Tianbao Soybean Food Technology Research Institute (hereinafter referred to as Tianbao Institute), dissatisfied with the civil judgment (2014) Jin Min Zhong Zi No. 141 rendered by the Shanxi High People's Court in the dispute over a technology contract with the respondent, Fenzhou Yuyuan Local Specialty Products Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Yuyuan Company), applied to this Court for retrial. This Court rendered the civil ruling (2015) Min Shen Zi No. 942 on January 13, 2016, granting retrial of this case. This Court formed a collegiate panel according to law and held a hearing. Guo Kai, the legal representative of the re-applicant Tianbao Institute, and its authorized agents Zhao Zhijie and Pan Xiaoping, as well as the authorized agents of the respondent Yuyuan Company, Jin Erlan and Wang Yanbiao, appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. This case is now concluded.

Tianbao Institute applied for retrial on the following grounds: (1) The second-instance judgment had unclear findings of fact. 1. Tianbao Institute had performed all its obligations under the "Patent Implementation License Contract" and the "Investment Cooperation Agreement" (collectively, the involved contracts). In June 2007, Yuyuan Company used the involved technology and equipment to produce qualified walnut lactic acid bacteria drinks. Its technical representative signed and accepted the "Technology and Technical Data Acceptance Certificate." The parties sealed samples and, using Yuyuan Company's introduction letter, had them tested at the Shanxi Food Quality Supervision and Inspection Center / National Agricultural and Sideline Products and Liquor Quality Supervision and Inspection Center, and the results were qualified. At this point, Tianbao Institute's obligations under the involved contracts had been fully performed. 2. The second-instance judgment made erroneous findings regarding the inspection report No. SJS20070516 (the 2007 Inspection Report) and the April 2008 "National Industrial Product Production License" (the 2008 Production License). After the technology and equipment for the patent "Walnut Lactic Acid Bacteria Drink and its Preparation Method" (the involved patent) were accepted as qualified by both Tianbao Institute and Yuyuan Company, Yuyuan Company sent samples of the walnut lactic acid bacteria drink for testing and obtained the 2007 Inspection Report, which showed that all indicators of the drink produced using the involved patented technology were qualified. Thereafter, Yuyuan Company began to default on the technology transfer fee payable to Tianbao Institute and, without Tianbao Institute's knowledge, applied for and obtained the 2008 Production License. This license sufficiently proves that Yuyuan Company obtained permission to produce walnut lactic acid bacteria drinks. The second-instance judgment, on the ground that the 2007 Inspection Report was submitted beyond the time limit for evidence, denied the fact that Yuyuan Company had obtained the 2008 Production License, which lacks basis. 3. The second-instance judgment made erroneous findings regarding the inspection report No. SJS20110747 (the 2011 Inspection Report) and the September 2011 "National Industrial Product Production License" (the 2011 Production License). After Yuyuan Company obtained the 2008 Production License in April 2008, it transferred the involved technology and equipment to Shanxi Fenzhou Yuyuan Food Co., Ltd. (Yuyuan Food Company). In 2011, Yuyuan Food Company again sampled and sent the walnut lactic acid bacteria drink for testing. The 2011 Inspection Report indicated that the submitted product was qualified. Subsequently, Yuyuan Food Company obtained the 2011 Production License. The second-instance judgment did not find this fact, which lacks basis. 4. The second-instance judgment's finding that the product had a poor taste and contained sediment lacks basis. Yuyuan Company claimed the product had poor taste and sediment, but it only made oral statements without any scientific testing basis, nor did it provide samples of unqualified drinks. It flatly refused Tianbao Institute's suggestion to use the involved equipment and technology to produce drinks and then test them, and dismantled all equipment, destroying evidence in this case. 5. The second-instance judgment found that the involved production license was irrelevant to the case on the ground that protein drinks and walnut lactic acid bacteria drinks are different, which lacks basis. First, the relevant inspection reports clearly indicate that the submitted samples were walnut lactic acid bacteria drinks. Second, beverages produced from protein-rich raw materials such as peanuts, walnuts, soybeans, and almonds all fall under the broad category of protein beverages. The product name column of the relevant production license will always record it as a protein beverage. (2) The second-instance court erred in applying the law. The second-instance court, finding that neither party was at fault and that Yuyuan Company's contractual purpose was frustrated, ordered Tianbao Institute to bear 80% of the liability, pay for the specialized equipment it procured on behalf of Yuyuan Company and the equipment Yuyuan Company purchased itself, and ordered Yuyuan Company to return the patented technology. This lacks basis. First, Tianbao Institute had fully performed its contractual obligations and provided evidence at the second instance proving that Yuyuan Company concealed facts such as the qualified test results of walnut lactic acid bacteria drink samples and the acquisition of the production license. Second, Tianbao Institute had transferred the right to use the patented technology to Yuyuan Company and taught it the methods of production and use, making the technology non-returnable. Finally, the non-standard specialized equipment was purchased by Tianbao Institute on behalf of Yuyuan Company, and the other ordinary equipment was purchased and used by Yuyuan Company itself. They should not be Tianbao Institute's responsibility. Tianbao Institute should not bear the risk of Yuyuan Company's inability to profit. (3) The second-instance court failed to address whether Yuyuan Company was a proper plaintiff in this case. In 2008, Yuyuan Company transferred the involved technology and equipment to Yuyuan Food Company. Thereafter, Yuyuan Company neither used the involved technology and equipment to produce products nor was it the actual owner of the involved technology and equipment. It had no right to participate in this lawsuit. (4) Yuyuan Company was the perpetrator of the infringing act and the party in breach of the involved contracts. Yuyuan Company's unauthorized transfer of the involved patented technology constituted infringement of the patent rights. Yuyuan Company's delay in paying the patent implementation license fee of RMB 600,000 under the involved contracts constituted a breach. In summary, the second-instance judgment had unclear findings of fact and erroneous application of law. Tianbao Institute requested the revocation of the second-instance judgment and an order that Yuyuan Company bear all litigation costs of this case.

Yuyuan Company argued in defense: (1) Tianbao Institute did not fully perform its obligations under the involved contracts. 1. The non-standard equipment customized by Tianbao Institute had serious quality problems. It did not inform Yuyuan Company of the manufacturer of the non-standard equipment, nor did it provide relevant invoices. During multiple rounds of communication between the parties, Tianbao Institute had already acknowledged the quality issues of the non-standard equipment. 2. The "Acceptance Certificate for Patent Technology and Technical Data" cannot prove that the contract has been fully performed. (1) The involved contracts stipulated that the parties should sign a "Contract Technology Acceptance and Qualification Agreement," not the "Acceptance Certificate for Patent Technology and Technical Data." (2) Tianbao Institute did not transfer the core patented technologies such as probiotic culture, domestication, and fermentation to Yuyuan Company; it only provided the starter culture during trial production. (3) Yuyuan Company did not authorize Wang Jianyun to sign the "Acceptance Certificate for Patent Technology and Technical Data." According to the memorandum and testimony provided by Wang Jianyun, the acceptance certificate was signed by him after being deceived by Guo Kai. Moreover, the first trial production on June 1, 2007, was still in progress, and the first four trial products were unqualified, making it impossible to conduct a technical acceptance at that time. (2) Qualified products could not be produced using the involved technology. 1. The burden of proving that qualified products could be produced using the involved patented technology rested with Tianbao Institute. The involved contracts explicitly required Tianbao Institute to install and debug the provided equipment until it operated normally and could produce qualified products. Therefore, whether the products were qualified should be proven by Tianbao Institute. 2. Tianbao Institute failed to prove that qualified products could be produced using the involved technology. (1) The 2007 Inspection Report cannot prove that Yuyuan Company produced qualified products using the involved patented technology. First, Guo Kai's act of submitting samples for testing did not comply with the sample submission procedures stipulated in the contract. Guo Kai did not receive authorization to submit samples for testing; his act was a personal act and unrelated to Yuyuan Company. Second, Yuyuan Company never produced samples with a 500 ml specification. (2) The 2008 Production License, the 2011 Inspection Report, and the 2011 Production License cannot prove that Yuyuan Company produced qualified products using the involved patented technology. First, the above inspection reports and production licenses were not evidence that Tianbao Institute could not obtain due to objective reasons during the first instance, so they do not constitute new evidence for the second instance. Second, the 2011 Inspection Report and the 2011 Production License were the submission report and production license of Yuyuan Food Company, unrelated to Yuyuan Company and also unrelated to the involved contracts. Third, after Tianbao Institute's personnel withdrew on July 16, 2007, there was no further cooperation between Yuyuan Company and Tianbao Institute. The product submitted for testing in the 2011 Inspection Report was not related to Tianbao Institute's patented technology. Moreover, the protein value in the 2007 Inspection Report was 1.15g/100g, while in the 2011 Inspection Report it was 0.7g/100g, indicating that the tested products were not the same. Finally, Tianbao Institute claimed that the protein content of walnut lactic acid bacteria drinks should be 15-20%, far exceeding the 0.6g/100g of ordinary protein drinks. Therefore, protein drinks and the walnut lactic acid bacteria drinks in this case are not the same technical products. The production license for protein drinks cannot prove the production situation of the involved walnut lactic acid bacteria drinks. 3. Yuyuan Company has evidence proving that qualified products could not be produced using the involved technology. Under the guidance of Tianbao Institute, Yuyuan Company conducted two rounds of trial production from May 26 to June 5, 2007, and from July 9 to July 16, 2007, totaling ten batches, but never obtained a qualified product. The trial products had problems such as unstable taste, sediment, layering, and black floating matter. On July 16, 2007, Tianbao Institute and Yuyuan Company summarized 23 problems in two aspects, and the representative of Tianbao Institute signed to acknowledge them. (3) Yuyuan Company is a proper plaintiff in this case. In this case, from the signing of the contract, to the payment of patent license fees and equipment costs, and to the trial production, all were completed by Yuyuan Company. Yuyuan Company has standing to sue. As for whether Yuyuan Food Company infringed Tianbao Institute's patent rights, it is unrelated to this case and should not be addressed in this case. (4) The second-instance court's judgment to terminate the involved contracts and order Tianbao Institute to bear the responsibility of returning the patent use fees and equipment costs was correct in law. 1. Tianbao Institute had already abandoned the cooperation. Yuyuan Company's request to terminate the contract was consistent with the intent of both parties. On April 12, 2011, Tianbao Institute sent a letter to Yuyuan Company stating, "The Institute is writing to inquire whether your company still intends to continue performing the original patent implementation license contract..." On May 25, 2011, Tianbao Institute sent another letter to Yuyuan Company stating, "Please indicate by June 15 whether our cooperation will continue and how to deal with the remaining issues. Otherwise, we will consider that you have abandoned the cooperation..." 2. Tianbao Company violated the contract by failing to make technical improvements to defective products. Yuyuan Company had the right to terminate the contract. The equipment provided by Tianbao Institute had no certificates, no invoices, its materials did not meet national standards, the mechanical manufacturing was crude, and it did not meet food production requirements; the proprietary non-standard equipment was unscientifically designed, unreasonably laid out, and some parts were obsolete and outdated; the trial products' performance did not meet the contract requirements and could not be used for industrial production, causing Yuyuan Company to be unable to commence production as scheduled, resulting in huge economic losses to Yuyuan Company. According to Articles 94, 349, and 351 of the Contract Law and Articles 5 and 10 of the involved contracts, Yuyuan Company had the right to terminate the contract, and Tianbao Institute should bear liability for breach of contract. (5) Tianbao Institute's other claims lack basis and are untenable. First, the claim that Yuyuan Company resolutely refused to allow Tianbao Institute personnel to use the equipment and technology to produce qualified drinks lacks basis. Yuyuan Company agreed to another trial production but believed that Tianbao Institute should bear the cost of the relevant raw materials. Therefore, the real reason the trial production could not proceed was that Tianbao Institute refused to bear the raw material costs. Second, the claim that Yuyuan Company dismantled all equipment to create the false impression that production could not take place lacks basis. Some equipment was damaged due to an accidental fire on the evening of May 20, 2013; Yuyuan Company did not intentionally damage the equipment. In summary, the second-instance judgment had clear findings of fact and correct application of law. Yuyuan Company requested that Tianbao Institute's application for retrial be dismissed.

Yuyuan Company filed a lawsuit with the Luliang Intermediate People's Court of Shanxi Province (the first-instance court) requesting: the termination of the "Patent Implementation License Contract" and the "Investment Cooperation Agreement" signed between Tianbao Institute and Yuyuan Company; an order that Tianbao Institute return the technology service fee of RMB 500,000 paid by Yuyuan Company; compensation for the loss of equipment purchased by Yuyuan Company amounting to RMB 1,237,900; and that Tianbao Institute bear the litigation costs of this case. The first-instance court found the following facts: On May 5, 2006, Yuyuan Company and Tianbao Institute signed the "Patent Implementation License Contract." The contract stipulated that Tianbao Institute would license the involved patent to Yuyuan Company for implementation. The main specific terms of the contract are as follows: (1) Patent technology content, requirements, and industrialization development procedures: 1. All processes, technologies, and procedures of the invention patent technology; 2. All formulas; 3. Copies of patent application materials; 4. Copies of appraisal materials; 5. Preliminary feasibility study report; 6. Sketches of plant renovation or construction, equipment layout, and process flow; 7. Hygiene and quality standards; 8. Customization of main equipment (prices detailed in the equipment schedule attached to the contract); 9. Responsible for training 1-3 core technical personnel until they can independently produce qualified products; 10. Install and debug the provided equipment until it operates normally and can produce qualified products; 11. Assist in building an inspection laboratory and train inspection personnel. (2) Submission deadline, location, and method for technical data: Within 180 days from the date the contract takes effect (i.e., after the down payment is made), Tianbao Institute shall provide Yuyuan Company with the items listed in (1) in Shanxi Province through correspondence, guidance, and practice. (3) Confidentiality scope: All processes, technologies, procedures, formulas, bacterial cultures, and equipment (equipment refers to the proprietary non-standard equipment provided by Tianbao Institute); confidentiality period: 20 years; violation shall be treated as infringement. (4) Type of patent implementation license: exclusive in Shanxi Province. (5) Acceptance standards and methods: After Yuyuan Company uses the technology and conducts trial production, if the products meet the technical performance indicators specified in this contract (hygiene and quality both at national standard level), the acceptance shall be carried out through a one-time practice method, and both parties shall sign a contract technology acceptance and qualification agreement. If the problem lies with the technology or the equipment provided by Tianbao Institute, Tianbao Institute shall be responsible for achieving compliance; if qualified products cannot be produced at all, Tianbao Institute shall bear the corresponding economic losses. If the problem lies with Yuyuan Company's management, environment, personnel, materials, facilities, etc., Yuyuan Company shall be responsible for correction. (6) Royalty fee and payment method: Payable in three installments. Total amount: RMB 1,100,000 (patent technology fee). Tianbao Institute contributes RMB 600,000 as capital. First installment: upon signing the contract, Yuyuan Company pays Tianbao Institute a down payment of RMB 100,000. When Tianbao Institute obtains the approved patent application number, Yuyuan Company pays another RMB 100,000. Second installment: when Yuyuan Company picks up the equipment, it pays Tianbao Institute RMB 200,000. Third installment: when the technology transfer is completed and Yuyuan Company independently produces qualified products, it pays another RMB 100,000. (7) Technical services: Service location: Shanxi Province. Service method: services through correspondence, guidance, and practice. Installation fee: calculated at 5% of the total equipment cost. Tianbao Institute shall not charge Yuyuan Company any other service fees. (10) Liquidated damages or calculation method for compensation for losses: If a party violates the provisions of Articles 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, or 14 of this contract, that party shall be deprived of the patent rights in Shanxi Province and shall pay cash. (14) Others: 6. Tianbao Institute shall grant Yuyuan Company the free use of the proprietary technology for soybean fiber lactic acid bacteria drinks. 7. Yuyuan Company agrees to pay Tianbao Institute the first installment of equipment ordering money before June 10, 2006, but the time for picking up the equipment shall be determined by Yuyuan Company. On May 6, 2006, Yuyuan Company and Tianbao Institute signed the "Investment Cooperation Agreement." The agreement stipulated that both parties would invest in establishing a walnut lactic acid bacteria drink production enterprise. (1) Investment form: Tianbao Institute contributes RMB 600,000 out of the RMB 1,100,000 transfer fee for the involved patent as its investment; Yuyuan Company contributes land use rights, plant, equipment, proprietary technology, and working capital as its investment. Tianbao Institute's contribution accounts for 15% of the enterprise's original shares, and Yuyuan Company's contribution accounts for 85% of the original shares. (4) Tianbao Institute shall, in accordance with the parties' agreement on the purchase of production equipment and upon Yuyuan Company's notice, transport all equipment to the completed workshop. Tianbao Institute shall be fully responsible for the quality of the equipment. Based on the evidence on record, the receipts for technology use fees, fund operation account statements, delivery details, cash vouchers, transfer vouchers, expense reimbursement forms, and value-added tax invoices submitted by Yuyuan Company are sufficient to prove that Yuyuan Company performed its contractual obligations; however, Tianbao Institute failed to prove that it performed its contractual obligations. The first-instance court ruled: (1) The "Patent Implementation License Contract" and the "Investment Cooperation Agreement" signed between Yuyuan Company and Tianbao Institute are terminated; (2) Tianbao Institute shall return the patent technology use fee of RMB 500,000 paid by Yuyuan Company; (3) Tianbao Institute shall return the equipment ordering money of RMB 655,100 paid by Yuyuan Company, and Yuyuan Company shall return the corresponding ordered equipment to Tianbao Institute; (4) Tianbao Institute shall compensate Yuyuan Company for the cost of self-purchased equipment of RMB 486,791, and Yuyuan Company shall deliver the corresponding self-purchased equipment to Tianbao Institute; (5) Tianbao Institute shall compensate Yuyuan Company for the research and development expenses invested in trial production of RMB 96,000; (6) Yuyuan Company's other claims are dismissed.

Tianbao Institute, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed, requesting: to set aside items 1 through 5 of the first-instance judgment, and to dismiss Yuyuan Company's claims. The Shanxi High People's Court (hereinafter referred to as the “second-instance court”) confirmed the facts as found by the first-instance court. The second-instance court additionally found: 1. Yuyuan Company was established in 1998 and is a production and sales enterprise primarily engaged in the research, development, and processing of agricultural and sideline products such as walnuts and walnut kernels. Tianbao Institute is a consulting company engaged in the research and development of new technologies and new products for soybean-based foods. It applied for the patent in question to the State Patent Office on May 22, 2006, and the patent was granted and announced on May 22, 2010. 2. The background for the conclusion of the patent exploitation license contract in this case was that the “Preliminary Feasibility Study on Walnut Lactic Acid Bacteria Beverage (Economic Analysis Section)” provided by Tianbao Institute to Yuyuan Company stated: The fermentation and emulsification technology of the walnut lactic acid bacteria beverage is domestically leading and internationally advanced, and is a world-first project filling an international gap. The beverage product has a delicate taste, pure flavor, and no stratification or precipitation. The project requires low investment with quick returns, and its return on investment is as high as 100-200%. 3. The acceptance standards and methods specified in the “Patent Exploitation License Contract” signed by both parties on May 5, 2006: an acceptance method of a one-time practical test, with both parties signing a contract technology acceptance qualification agreement. If the product fails acceptance and the issue is attributable to the technology and equipment provided, Tianbao Institute shall be responsible for bringing it up to standard; if a qualified product cannot be produced despite all efforts, Tianbao Institute shall bear the corresponding economic losses. 4. On December 2, 2006, after the non-standard equipment ordered by Tianbao Institute was delivered to Yuyuan Company's production workshop, the parties continuously negotiated, through meeting minutes and correspondence, regarding the equipment quality issues and technical problems arising during trial production, until as late as August 29, 2012, when Tianbao Institute sent a letter to Yuyuan Company still discussing matters such as returning the equipment. 5. On April 14, 2007, the walnut lactic acid bacteria beverage and its preparation method provided by Yuyuan Company passed the scientific and technological achievement appraisal organized by the Luliang Science and Technology Bureau. 6. On June 1, 2007, the document signed by Wang Jianyun, the person receiving the technology and materials on Yuyuan Company's side, was the “Patent Technology and Technical Data Acceptance Certificate” rather than the contract technology acceptance qualification agreement as stipulated in the patent exploitation license contract. 7. Around June and July 2007, the walnut lactic acid bacteria beverage produced in trial batches was sent to local hotels for free tasting, but it still could not be marketed for sale due to problems such as unstable taste and unresolved precipitation. 8. On August 11, 2014, the collegiate panel of the second-instance court, together with the parties, went to the walnut lactic acid bacteria production workshop for a joint on-site inspection of the equipment and trial production status. All equipment involved in the case, as acknowledged by both parties, was in a state of disuse; the production line had been dismantled, and part of the workshop had been repurposed. 9. Tianbao Institute did not transfer the proprietary technology of soybean fiber lactic acid bacteria beverage to Yuyuan Company for use free of charge as agreed.

The second-instance court held: The purpose of the patent exploitation license contract for the walnut lactic acid bacteria beverage and its preparation method signed by Yuyuan Company and Tianbao Institute was to produce the walnut lactic acid bacteria beverage as promised by Tianbao Institute through implementing the patented technology, and to market it for sale, thereby realizing the enterprise's investment profit. The root cause of the dispute in this case was that the trial-produced walnut lactic acid bacteria beverage failed to achieve industrial production and market launch due to inconsistent taste and the presence of sediment. The production line established by Yuyuan Company for implementing the patented technology was abandoned because it could not resolve the product's quality issues. After six years of continuous negotiation over the implementation of the patented technology, the parties ultimately resorted to litigation because no qualified product meeting market conditions could be produced. After signing the patent exploitation license contract, Yuyuan Company paid Tianbao Institute a technology usage fee of RMB 500,000 in seven installments as agreed, and equipment costs for non-standard equipment and general equipment totaling RMB 1,141,891, completed the civil works for the project, and fulfilled its obligations under the patent exploitation license contract. There is no evidence showing that Yuyuan Company breached the contract during the cooperation between the parties. As the licensor under the patent exploitation license contract, Tianbao Institute, after the non-standard equipment it ordered was delivered to Yuyuan Company's production workshop in December 2006, disputes arose between the parties over the quality of that equipment. During the process of continually improving the equipment and conducting trial production of the walnut lactic acid bacteria beverage, Tianbao Institute was never able to resolve the problems of unstable taste and sedimentation in the trial-produced beverage, resulting in the parties' failure to jointly sign the contract technology acceptance qualification agreement in accordance with the acceptance standards and methods stipulated in the contract. Moreover, upon the on-site inspection of the production workshop by the collegiate panel and both parties, all equipment involved in the case was found to be in a state of disuse. Accordingly, it can be determined that Tianbao Institute did not complete its contractual obligations as agreed, and the losses suffered by Yuyuan Company due to its investment in implementing the patented technology are evident. During the second-instance proceedings, the evidence submitted by Tianbao Institute was insufficient to prove that it had performed its contractual obligations: (1) The science and technology achievement appraisal certificate for the walnut lactic acid bacteria beverage and its preparation method issued by the Luliang Science and Technology Bureau in April 2007 was an appraisal of its patented method, and at the time the certificate was issued, no trial production had yet been conducted; this certificate cannot be used as evidence of the results of implementing the patent in this case. (2) The inspection report for the walnut lactic acid bacteria beverage submitted for testing by the legal representative of Tianbao Institute itself in 2007; Yuyuan Company did not recognize the authenticity of this inspection report because it was done solely by Tianbao Institute and did not comply with the testing and submission procedures agreed in the contract. (3) The inspection reports for protein beverages, production license, hygiene license, production barcode, and other evidence owned by Yuyuan Company were all procedures perfected by Yuyuan Company for producing protein beverages. Protein beverage production is a relatively mature technology, and such beverages are widely produced and sold in the domestic market. However, the fermentation and emulsification technology used in the production of the walnut lactic acid bacteria beverage in this case belongs to domestically and even internationally leading technology. Clearly, the protein beverages referred to in this set of evidence are not the same type of technological product as the walnut lactic acid bacteria beverage in this case. (4) The promotional materials regarding the production and sale of walnut lactic acid bacteria beverage downloaded from Yuyuan Company's internet promotional page through notarization by Tianbao Institute were used to prove that the product in question had been mass-produced and marketed. This set of evidence is merely a form of enterprise promotion by Yuyuan Company, and it actually confirms Yuyuan Company's sincerity in cooperation and its desire for the product to be launched on the market. However, the result of the cooperation between the parties was that the trial production line had been abandoned, and no walnut lactic acid bacteria beverage could be found in the production workshop or on the current market. Therefore, Tianbao Institute's appeal contention that it had completed its contractual obligations and achieved the purpose of the contract lacks a factual basis. Regarding the investment cooperation agreement signed by the parties, from December 2, 2006, until the filing of this lawsuit by Yuyuan Company, the parties continuously negotiated over the quality issues of the non-standard equipment and whether the trial-produced products were qualified. Since industrial production and market launch of the product as agreed in the contract were not achieved, there was no issue of the parties establishing a new company through investment. In summary, because the purpose of Yuyuan Company in signing the contract in this case was frustrated, it was not improper for the first-instance court to rule that the parties should rescind the contract and that Tianbao Institute should refund the patent technology usage fee of RMB 500,000 it had received. The implementation of the patented technology in this case did not produce a product meeting the conditions for industrial production as stipulated in the contract, which indeed caused significant losses to Yuyuan Company. However, neither party had subjective fault for the occurrence of this result. In accordance with the principle of fairness, an appropriate adjustment was made to the compensation for losses portion of the first-instance judgment: Yuyuan Company shall bear 20% of the loss liability, i.e., (655,100 + 486,791 + 96,000) x 20% = RMB 247,578.2; Tianbao Institute shall bear the remaining 80% of the loss compensation liability, i.e., RMB 990,312.8. The second-instance court ruled: (1) Affirmed items 1, 2, and 6 of the first-instance judgment; (2) Set aside items 3, 4, and 5 of the first-instance judgment; (3) Modified the judgment: Tianbao Institute shall compensate Yuyuan Company for equipment ordering costs, self-purchased equipment costs, and research and development expenses totaling RMB 990,312.8, and Yuyuan Company shall return the corresponding equipment to Tianbao Institute.

Regarding the parties' retrial requests, this Court finds and determines the disputed evidence and facts as follows:

(1) Whether the “2007 Inspection Report” should be admitted as evidence

Tianbao Institute submitted the “2007 Inspection Report” during the first-instance proceedings of this case, intending to prove that Yuyuan Company had produced qualified products using the patented technology in question. According to the record of this inspection report, Guo Kai, entrusted by Yuyuan Company, sent the walnut lactic acid bacteria beverage produced by that company to the Shanxi Provincial Food Quality Supervision and Inspection Center for inspection on June 14, 2007. The specification of the submitted sample was 500 ml. The inspection conclusion was: “1. A total of 12 items were inspected, and all 12 items were qualified; 2. According to the judgment under standards QB1554-1992 and GB16321-2003: The sample meets the requirements for the inspected items.” Yuyuan Company argued that Guo Kai's submission of the sample was his personal act, unrelated to Yuyuan Company; that the submission procedure did not comply with the agreement in the letter of December 9, 2006, between the parties; and that Yuyuan Company had never produced a sample with a specification of 500 ml. Therefore, Yuyuan Company argued that the “2007 Inspection Report” should not be admitted as evidence.

This Court found through trial: Tianbao Institute sent a letter to Fenyuan Yuyuan Biotechnology Co., Ltd. on December 9, 2006, with the letter also “submitted to Chairman Yu.” The letter stated, “According to the provisions of the contract between the parties, we propose the following handling opinions regarding the problems with the non-standard equipment provided by our institute: ... 2. ... After producing qualified products, Party B shall organize testing. ... If you agree with our plan, we will proceed with the implementation plan. ...” Yu Cuiping wrote an instruction on the letter: “... evaluate and make a plan as soon as possible.” Although the addressee of the letter was Fenyuan Yuyuan Biotechnology Co., Ltd. rather than Yuyuan Company, given that the letter was also submitted to Yuyuan Company's legal representative Yu Cuiping and that the content of the letter clearly pertained to the contract in question, the content of the letter should still be examined. Because the content of the letter was merely a proposal from Tianbao Institute, which was still subject to confirmation by Yuyuan Company, absent other evidence proving that Yuyuan Company and Tianbao Institute had reached an agreement on the related plan, the instruction by Yu Cuiping alone is insufficient to establish that Yuyuan Company had accepted the plan set out in the letter. In other words, based on the existing evidence, it is difficult to ascertain that the parties agreed that product testing must be organized by Yuyuan Company. Moreover, even if it were determined that Yuyuan Company and Tianbao Institute had reached an agreement on product testing being organized by Yuyuan Company, given that at the time of this sample submission, Yuyuan Company and Tianbao Institute were still in close cooperation, and given that the “2007 Inspection Report” explicitly recorded “Entrusting entity: Shanxi Fenyuan Yuyuan Native Produce Trading Co., Ltd.,” in the absence of sufficient counter-evidence submitted by Yuyuan Company, it should be determined that Guo Kai submitted the sample on behalf of Yuyuan Company, and that his act of submission was not a personal act and did not constitute a violation of the parties' agreement. Regarding Yuyuan Company's contention that it had never produced a product with a specification of 500 ml, this Court holds that, given the high probability that the product specification was still uncertain during the trial production phase, and in the absence of other contrary evidence provided by Yuyuan Company, it is difficult to determine that the submitted product was not Yuyuan Company's product. Therefore, Yuyuan Company's contention is not supported by this Court.

In summary, this Court holds that the “2007 Inspection Report” should be admitted as evidence.

(2) Whether the “Patent Technology and Technical Data Acceptance Certificate” should be admitted as evidence

Tianbao Institute submitted the “Patent Technology and Technical Data Acceptance Certificate” during the first-instance proceedings, intending to prove that it had performed its relevant obligations under the contract in question. Article 1 of the certificate states: “Party A has, as entrusted by the legal representative of Party B, Chairman Yu, imparted all the technology (including core technology) of the project, namely the walnut lactic acid bacteria beverage and its preparation method, to the designated patent technology recipient, Director Wang Jianyun, who has (independently) used the patented technology to produce products that meet the national standard (GB16321-2003) and industry standard (QB1554-92).” Article 2 states: “Party A has handed over the top-secret information—the preparation method, formula, and other items (referring to the relevant technical data on the bacterial strain) to the designated recipient of Party A, Director Wang Jianyun.” Guo Kai and Wang Jianyun signed the certificate. Yuyuan Company claimed that Wang Jianyun signed the certificate under deception, and therefore the “Patent Technology and Technical Data Acceptance Certificate” should not be admitted as evidence.

This Court found through trial: During the first-instance proceedings, Yuyuan Company had already submitted a memorandum handwritten by Wang Jianyun, titled “Memorandum on the Cooperation between Yuyuan Company and Xi'an Soybean Research Institute for the Walnut Lactic Acid Beverage Project.” The memorandum states: “My name is Wang Jianyun. I am a member of the preparatory team for Yuyuan Company's walnut lactic acid bacteria beverage project. I am responsible for the production of the walnut lactic acid bacteria beverage and the patented technology, and also assist Party A in the installation and debugging of mechanical equipment...” This Court holds that, in light of Wang Jianyun's own statement, it is sufficient to determine that the content confirmed by him in the “Patent Technology and Technical Data Acceptance Certificate” was consistent with his scope of responsibilities, and his act of signing the certificate was an act performed in the course of his employment. Yuyuan Company's claim that Wang Jianyun signed under fraud lacks evidentiary support and is not upheld by this Court.

In summary, this Court holds that the “Patent Technology and Technical Data Acceptance Certificate” should be admitted as evidence.

(3) Whether the “2008 Production License,” “2011 Inspection Report,” and “2011 Production License” should be admitted as evidence

Tianbao Institute submitted the “2008 Production License,” “2011 Inspection Report,” and “2011 Production License” during the second-instance proceedings to further prove that Yuyuan Company could produce qualified products using the patented technology in question. Yuyuan Company argued that none of the above evidence should be admitted, mainly on the following grounds: First, none of the above evidence was evidence that could not be obtained during the first-instance proceedings due to objective reasons, so they do not constitute new evidence for the second instance; second, the “2011 Inspection Report” and “2011 Production License” both refer to Yuyuan Food Company, which is unrelated to Yuyuan Company; third, the protein beverages referred to in the production licenses are not the same type of technological product as the walnut lactic acid bacteria beverage, so it cannot be determined that the said production licenses pertain to the walnut lactic acid bacteria beverage in this case.

This Court holds that the inspected entity in the “2011 Inspection Report” and the licensee in the “2011 Production License” are both Yuyuan Food Company. Although Tianbao Institute claimed that Yuyuan Company had transferred the technology and equipment in question to Yuyuan Food Company, it did not submit sufficient evidence to prove this. Therefore, the “2011 Inspection Report” and “2011 Production License” lack relevance to this case and are not admitted by this Court. Given that during the retrial hearing, Yuyuan Company explicitly acknowledged that the walnut lactic acid bacteria beverage falls under the category of protein beverages, and in accordance with Article 65, paragraph 2 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 102 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China concerning the rules for admitting delayed evidence, this Court holds that the “2008 Production License” should be admitted as evidence.

This Court holds in the retrial: Based on the first-instance judgment, second-instance judgment, and the grounds for retrial raised by Tianbao Institute, the main point of dispute in this case is: Whether the contract in question may be rescinded pursuant to Article 94(4) of the Contract Law.

Article 94 of the Contract Law establishes the system of statutory right to rescind a contract. The primary purpose of this system is, of course, to grant the non-breaching party the right to rescind the contract, so that it may obtain special relief in the form of rescission as a remedy. However, as a system under the Contract Law, the right to rescind must necessarily be premised on the legislative purpose and value orientation of the Contract Law, which is to uphold autonomy of will, encourage market transactions, stabilize market order, and achieve efficient allocation of resources. Therefore, strict limitation of the conditions for exercising the statutory right to rescind is the main aspect and value emphasis of this system. Rescission of a contract is not the only remedy for breach of contract, nor is it an automatic remedy. If contracts could be easily rescinded, and transactional relationships easily aborted, it would inevitably lead to chaos in market order, inflated transaction costs, and inefficient resource allocation. Thus, although according to Article 94(4) of the Contract Law, if one party delays performance of its obligations or commits other breaches causing the purpose of the contract to be frustrated, the other party has the right to rescind the contract; it must be clarified that only when the breach is so serious as to cause the purpose of the contract to be frustrated is there room for applying the remedy of rescission. In other words, the exercise of the statutory right to rescind under this provision requires that the breach by one party result in the frustration of the contract's purpose. In summary, to realize the primary value of the statutory right to rescind system, Article 94(4) of the Contract Law must be strictly applied. To strictly apply this provision, the key is to correctly determine the purpose of the contract and avoid expanding the interpretation of the contract's purpose beyond the true consensus of the parties.

In the field of technology contracts, especially contracts involving the industrialization of technology, special attention should be paid to strictly regulating the application of the statutory right to rescind. Industrialization is a critical stage in the transformation of science and technology into productive forces. From the laboratory to the factory, from trial production to mass production, overcoming known and unknown difficulties through repeated debugging and continuous improvement is an inevitable path for technology industrialization. In this process, sincere cooperation between the investor and the technology provider is urgently needed to ultimately achieve the transformation of scientific and technological achievements and innovation-driven development. Therefore, the determination of whether a breach in the performance of such a contract constitutes a fundamental breach should be particularly cautious:

First, it must be clarified that whether the purpose of the contract is frustrated is the criterion for determining the possibility of exercising the statutory right to rescind. Under China's Contract Law, the standard for determining statutory rescission is whether the consequences of the breach are sufficiently serious, rather than whether the breached clause itself is important. Although there may be a logical connection between the two, emphasizing the seriousness of the consequences of the breach as the focal point for determining statutory rescission is itself a limitation on the statutory right to rescind. Therefore, when determining whether a breach is sufficient to warrant statutory rescission of the contract, one cannot simply infer fundamental breach from the nature of the clause breached; rather, it must be examined whether this breach results in the frustration of the contract's purpose.

Secondly, where there is no explicit agreement, the commercialization of a product should not be deemed as the purpose of a technology contract. Product commercialization is a concept different from technical industrialization. Technical industrialization aims at the industrial application of a technology, addressing only the issue of whether a technology can move from the laboratory to the factory and produce qualified products. Product commercialization, on the other hand, aims at profitability and concerns whether supply and demand match in terms of quality and quantity, that is, whether the product is marketable and profitable. Admittedly, technical industrialization should take product commercialization as its ultimate goal and orientation and should serve product commercialization. The closer the technical indicators set in technical industrialization are to market requirements, the greater the likelihood of success in product commercialization. However, technical industrialization is merely a necessary condition for product commercialization, not a sufficient one. Achieving product commercialization also requires meeting other conditions unrelated to the technology, such as accurately analyzing market demand, skillfully devising marketing strategies, strictly controlling production and sales costs, and ensuring the flow of funds. Moreover, setting precise technical indicators based on market demand is inherently extremely difficult. In practice, instances where technical industrialization succeeds but product commercialization fails are not uncommon. Therefore, if, in the absence of explicit agreement, product commercialization, or even profitability, is regarded as the contractual purpose of a technology contract, this would undoubtedly impose an unbearable burden on the technology and ultimately hinder the transformation of technology into productive forces. Hence, in the field of technology contracts, an expansive interpretation of the contractual purpose should be especially avoided — whether a product that meets the contractual specifications can be produced and whether that product can be marketed, is marketable, and is profitable are fundamentally issues at different levels. In the absence of explicit agreement, product commercialization should not be deemed the contractual purpose of a technology contract.

In this case, the issue of whether the contract signed between Tianbao Institute and Yuyuan Company can be rescinded pursuant to Article 94(4) of the Contract Law should be analyzed from the following three aspects: first, whether Tianbao Institute breached the contract; second, whether the contractual purpose cannot be achieved; and third, if Tianbao Institute did indeed constitute a breach and the contractual purpose indeed cannot be achieved, whether there is a causal relationship between the two. Therefore, the first matter to examine is whether Tianbao Institute breached the contractual obligations. In this case, according to Yuyuan Company's assertions, the determination of whether Tianbao Institute breached the contract should mainly be examined from three aspects: whether the product was qualified, whether the equipment was qualified, and whether the technology transfer was complete.

(1) Whether Yuyuan Company could produce qualified products using the patented technology in question

1. The standard for determining qualified products under the contract in question is the national standard.

Before determining whether Yuyuan Company could produce qualified products using the patented technology in question, the standard for qualified products under the contract in question must first be clarified. Article 1(9) of the contract in question states: "Responsible for training 1-3 core technical personnel, guiding them until they can independently produce qualified products (in compliance with national standards)." Article 5(1) states: "Party B, after using the technology and conducting trial production, has met the technical performance indicators specified in this contract (hygiene and quality are both national standards). Acceptance shall be carried out using a one-time practice method, and both parties shall sign a contract technology acceptance agreement." The above clauses are clearly expressed, unambiguous, and mutually corroborative. Therefore, this Court determines that the standard for qualified products under the contract in question is the national standard.

Yuyuan Company asserts that the walnut lactobacillus beverage products produced using the patented technology in question have problems such as unstable taste, sedimentation, layering, and black floating matter, and thus are unqualified products. This Court holds that, irrespective of whether Yuyuan Company has sufficient evidence to prove the existence of the above problems, given that the standard for qualified products under the contract in question is the national standard, and where Yuyuan Company has not clarified whether taste, sedimentation, layering, and black floating matter are included in the inspection items of the national standards for the hygiene and quality of walnut lactobacillus beverages, the presence or absence of the above problems cannot be used to determine whether the products under the contract in question are qualified. The determination of whether the products under the contract are qualified must be based on the national standards explicitly agreed upon by Yuyuan Company and Tianbao Institute.

2. The evidence on record is sufficient to prove that Yuyuan Company could use the patented technology in question to produce walnut lactobacillus beverage products that comply with national standards.

First, the "2007 Inspection Report" is sufficient to prove that Yuyuan Company could use the patented technology in question to produce walnut lactobacillus beverage products that comply with national standards. According to Yuyuan Company's own account, from May 26, 2007 to June 5, 2007, it conducted the first batch of five trial productions under the guidance of Tianbao Institute. On June 14, 2007, Guo Kai, on behalf of Yuyuan Company, sent the trial products to the Shanxi Provincial Food Quality Supervision and Inspection Center for testing. The Center issued the "2007 Inspection Report" on July 3, 2007. The report clearly states that the samples submitted by Yuyuan Company complied with the national standard for lactobacillus beverages (GB16321-2003) and the light industry standard (QB1554-1992).

Second, the "Patent Technology and Technical Materials Acceptance Certificate" constitutes Yuyuan Company's admission that it could use the patented technology in question to produce walnut lactobacillus products that comply with national standards. The acceptance certificate clearly states: "Party A has, as entrusted by Party B's legal representative, Chairman Yu, transferred all the technology (including core technology) of the project, namely walnut lactobacillus beverage and its preparation method, to the designated patent technology recipient, Director Wang Jianyun, who has used (independently) the patented technology to produce products that comply with the national standard (GB16321-2003) and the industry standard (QB1554-92)." Yuyuan Company asserts that this "Patent Technology and Technical Materials Acceptance Certificate" is not the "contract technology acceptance agreement" referred to in Article 5(1) of the contract in question, and therefore cannot prove the performance of the contract. This Court holds that the issue of whether the acceptance certificate constitutes the "contract technology acceptance agreement" agreed upon in the contract does not affect the determination of whether Yuyuan Company admitted that it could use the patented technology in question to produce walnut lactobacillus beverage products that comply with national standards. Yuyuan Company's above assertion clearly lacks a basis and is not supported by this Court.

Furthermore, the "2008 Production License" can also corroborate the above conclusion that Yuyuan Company could use the patented technology in question to produce qualified walnut lactobacillus beverages.

In summary, Tianbao Institute's assertion that Yuyuan Company could use the patented technology in question to produce qualified products has a factual basis and is supported by this Court. Yuyuan Company's contrary assertion lacks a basis and is not supported by this Court.

(2) Whether the equipment custom-made by Tianbao Institute was qualified

According to Article 1(8) and (10) of the contract in question: "...8. Customization of main equipment (prices are detailed in the equipment schedule attached to this contract); ...10. Install and commission the provided equipment until it operates normally and can produce qualified products (installation shall be carried out according to national regulations); ..." Therefore, under the contract in question, the standard for determining whether the customized equipment is qualified is whether it can operate normally and produce qualified products. As discussed above, Yuyuan Company could use the equipment custom-made by Tianbao Institute to produce qualified products, so the relevant equipment should be deemed qualified.

As for Yuyuan Company's assertion that Tianbao Institute has admitted that its equipment had problems. This Court holds that Yuyuan Company did indeed list 14 problems with the equipment in its document "Problems in the Lactobacillus Beverage Workshop"; Zhao Zhijie, the Party Branch Secretary of Tianbao Institute, also signed at the end of that document, but his specific statement was: "Received one copy of materials listing a total of 23 problems in two aspects. After reporting to Director Guo, it was issued." That is, Zhao Zhijie only indicated receipt of the materials, and his statement does not constitute an acknowledgment of the problems listed by Yuyuan Company. Tianbao Institute's reply to this document merely stated: "...with regard to the reasonable opinions you raised concerning the process and equipment, our institute has the ability to assist in resolving them..." It did not specifically indicate which opinions were "reasonable opinions," so this reply also does not constitute a clear acknowledgment of the problems listed by Yuyuan Company. Moreover, as stated above, the standard for determining whether equipment is qualified is whether it can produce qualified products. Therefore, given that it has been confirmed that qualified products can be produced, even if there are still defects in the equipment, that is insufficient to negate the conclusion that it constitutes qualified equipment.

In summary, Tianbao Institute's assertion that the equipment it custom-made was qualified has a factual basis and is supported by this Court. Yuyuan Company's assertion that the equipment custom-made by Tianbao Institute was unqualified lacks a basis and is not supported by this Court.

(3) Whether Tianbao Institute transferred the core patented technology to Yuyuan Company

Yuyuan Company asserts that Tianbao Institute did not transfer core patented technologies such as probiotic culture, domestication, and fermentation to Yuyuan Company. However, the "Patent Technology and Technical Materials Acceptance Certificate" signed and confirmed by Wang Jianyun, a member of the preparatory group for Yuyuan Company's walnut lactobacillus beverage project and the technical director, clearly states: "Party A has, as entrusted by Party B's legal representative, Chairman Yu, transferred all the technology (including core technology) of the project, namely walnut lactobacillus beverage and its preparation method, to the designated patent technology recipient, Director Wang Jianyun... Party A has delivered the top-secret materials — the walnut lactobacillus beverage preparation method, formula, and other materials (referring to the technical materials related to the bacterial strain) to the designated recipient of Party A, Director Wang Jianyun." Therefore, Yuyuan Company's assertion that Tianbao Institute did not transfer the core patented technology to Yuyuan Company clearly lacks a basis and is not supported by this Court.

In summary, Tianbao Institute did not engage in the breaches of contract alleged by Yuyuan Company. Therefore, Yuyuan Company's assertion that it could not achieve the contractual purpose due to Tianbao Institute's breach lacks a basis and is not supported by this Court. Yuyuan Company may not rescind the contract in question pursuant to Article 94(4) of the Contract Law, nor can it obtain the return of related fees or compensation. The court of second instance erred by using "meeting market launch conditions" as the basis for determining that the product was qualified, thereby elevating the technical standard agreed in the contract to a market standard. This constituted a misinterpretation of the clauses in the contract concerning the standard for qualified products. Its determination that Tianbao Institute breached the contract because it had always failed to resolve issues such as unstable taste and sedimentation in the trial products was erroneous, and this Court corrects that. Furthermore, the court of second instance's determination that Yuyuan Company's contractual purpose was to industrially produce walnut lactobacillus beverages using the patented technology in question and to market and sell them for profit was also improper. This Court holds that, as discussed above, in the absence of explicit agreement, product commercialization should not be deemed the contractual purpose of a technology contract. Given that the contract in question contains no agreement concerning the marketing and sale of the product, the contractual purpose should only be determined as the industrial production of walnut lactobacillus beverages that comply with national standards using the patented technology in question. As for Tianbao Institute's assertion that Yuyuan Company is not a proper plaintiff in this case, it clearly lacks a basis and is not supported by this Court. Tianbao Institute's assertion that Yuyuan Company infringed its patent rights pertains to a different legal relationship outside the scope of this case, and this Court does not comment on it.

This Court holds that investors should exercise caution when entering into contracts involving technical industrialization. In setting technical indicators and selecting product qualification standards, they should, as much as possible, keep close to the market's requirements for the product. They should particularly avoid, in areas where market competition is intense or where the relevant public has high expectations, using only market access standards as the product qualification standard under the contract, thereby falling into the predicament of having a product that meets technical standards but fails commercially.

In conclusion, Tianbao Institute's retrial request is meritorious. Pursuant to Article 207(1) and Article 170(1)(ii) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 94(4) of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

1. The civil judgment (2014) Jin Min Zhong Zi No. 141 of the Shanxi High People's Court is hereby set aside.

2. The civil judgment (2013) Lu Min San Chu Zi No. 1 of the Lvliang Intermediate People's Court of Shanxi Province is hereby set aside.

3. All claims of Fenzhou Yuyuan Local Specialty Products Co., Ltd. are dismissed.

Court acceptance fee of RMB 20,441 for the first instance shall be borne by Fenzhou Yuyuan Local Specialty Products Co., Ltd.; court acceptance fee of RMB 20,441 for the second instance shall be borne by Fenzhou Yuyuan Local Specialty Products Co., Ltd.

This judgment is final.
